title: Third Word Worship And Happiness Sin And Loss The Two Soldiers

questions.question: In the story, what were the two soldiers told to do?
questions.answer: They were told to go to a faraway city.

questions.question: What was at the place where the road split into two?
questions.answer: A man was there to explain the two roads.

questions.question: Which road was said to bring safety and good gain to most travelers?
questions.answer: The road on the right.

questions.question: Which road was said to bring loss to most travelers?
questions.answer: The road on the left.

questions.question: What was special about the left-hand road?
questions.answer: It had no rules and no leader over the travelers.

questions.question: What did the travelers on the left not have to carry?
questions.answer: They did not carry supplies and weapons.

questions.question: What did the travelers on the right have to carry?
questions.answer: They had to carry a bag of food and a strong rifle.

questions.question: Why might the left road look easier at first?
questions.answer: It seemed lighter because there was nothing to carry.

questions.question: Which soldier chose the right-hand road?
questions.answer: The fortunate soldier chose it.

questions.question: What happened to the fortunate soldier’s heart and spirit after choosing that road?
questions.answer: He was saved from great fear and from needing people too much.

questions.question: Why did the other soldier leave the army way?
questions.answer: He did not want to obey the rules.

questions.question: Even though the other soldier carried less, what heavy troubles did he get inside?
questions.answer: He felt deep fear and a heavy sense of owing others.

questions.question: How did the luckless soldier travel on the left road?
questions.answer: He kept asking people for help and was scared of many things.

questions.question: What happened to the luckless soldier when he arrived?
questions.answer: He was punished for turning against the army and running away.

questions.question: What happened to the soldier who stayed obedient and kept his gear?
questions.answer: He reached the city peacefully and got a reward.

questions.question: What two things does the passage compare?
questions.answer: It compares worship and sin by using a story.

questions.question: Who are the main people in the story?
questions.answer: Two soldiers.

questions.question: What choice did the soldiers face on their trip?
questions.answer: They had to choose between two different roads.

questions.question: What did the man say about most people who take the right road?
questions.answer: Most of them gain something good and feel peaceful.

questions.question: What did the man say about most people who take the left road?
questions.answer: Most of them lose out.

questions.question: Besides distance, what big difference was there between the two roads?
questions.answer: One road had order and authority, and the other did not.

questions.question: Why did the right road require more effort from the soldiers?
questions.answer: They had to carry food and a weapon.

questions.question: What choice did the lucky soldier make after hearing the warning?
questions.answer: He chose the right road.

questions.question: What choice did the unlucky soldier make?
questions.answer: He chose the left road and quit the army way.

questions.question: Did that free choice bring real comfort to him in the end?
questions.answer: No. It brought fear, need, and trouble.

questions.question: How was the obedient soldier different during the journey?
questions.answer: He traveled calmly, with no need to beg and no fear of others.

questions.question: What does the punishment of the second soldier help us understand?
questions.answer: Leaving duty and rebelling has bad results.

questions.question: What does the reward of the first soldier help us understand?
questions.answer: Faithful obedience brings honor and goodness.

questions.question: What does the passage say can be found in worship?
questions.answer: Great good and happiness.

questions.question: What does the passage say can be found in sinful living and wild behavior?
questions.answer: Great loss and ruin.

questions.question: What kind of story is used to teach this lesson?
questions.answer: A comparison story.

questions.question: How were the two soldiers alike at the beginning?
questions.answer: They both got the same order and started together.

questions.question: When did their paths become different?
questions.answer: When they came to the fork in the road.

questions.question: Who helped them understand the choices before them?
questions.answer: A man standing at the fork.

questions.question: What made the road on the right harder on the outside?
questions.answer: The soldier had to carry equipment.

questions.question: What made the road on the left seem easier on the outside?
questions.answer: The soldier did not have to carry those things.

questions.question: What hidden problem came with the left road?
questions.answer: It led to fear, need, and loss.

questions.question: What hidden blessing came with the right road?
questions.answer: It brought peace, safety, and success.

questions.question: How do we know the soldier on the right respected order?
questions.answer: He kept the rules and carried what he was told to carry.

questions.question: How do we know the soldier on the left was rebellious?
questions.answer: He left the army path and refused the rules.

questions.question: What happened to the rebellious soldier’s feelings as he traveled?
questions.answer: He became afraid and burdened inside.

questions.question: What happened to the obedient soldier’s feelings as he traveled?
questions.answer: He felt at ease and untroubled.

questions.question: What can we infer about rules from this story?
questions.answer: Good rules can protect us and help us.

questions.question: Why were the soldiers traveling?
questions.answer: They were under orders to go to another city.

questions.question: What message did the man at the fork give about the right road?
questions.answer: It was safe from loss and usually led to benefit and peace.

questions.question: What message did he give about the left road?
questions.answer: It had no real gain and usually ended in loss.

questions.question: Did both roads take the same amount of travel time?
questions.answer: Yes, the distance was the same.

questions.question: What two items did the right-road traveler carry?
questions.answer: A food bag and a rifle.

questions.question: What does the rifle show about that road?
questions.answer: It shows the traveler would be protected against enemies.

questions.question: What does the food bag show about that road?
questions.answer: It shows he had what he needed for the journey.

questions.question: What seemed good about the left road at first?
questions.answer: It felt lighter and freer.

questions.question: What was the real cost of that choice?
questions.answer: The soldier became needy, frightened, and guilty.

questions.question: How did the rebellious soldier depend on other people?
questions.answer: He had to beg from them.

questions.question: Why was the obedient soldier not forced to do that?
questions.answer: He was prepared and followed the right path.

questions.question: What happened at the end to show that choices have consequences?
questions.answer: One soldier was punished, and the other was rewarded.

questions.question: Which soldier had peace in both his heart and his trip?
questions.answer: The obedient soldier on the right road.

questions.question: Which soldier followed what only looked easy?
questions.answer: The luckless soldier on the left road.

questions.question: What does the passage ask the listener to understand before the story begins?
questions.answer: That worship brings good, while sinful living brings harm.

questions.question: What were the soldiers doing when they came to the fork?
questions.answer: They were traveling together.

questions.question: What information did the man give them about the two roads?
questions.answer: He told them the likely results and the difference between them.

questions.question: On which road did most people do well?
questions.answer: On the road to the right.

questions.question: On which road did most people end up badly?
questions.answer: On the road to the left.

questions.question: What kind of road had rules and authority?
questions.answer: The right-hand road.

questions.question: What kind of road had no rules and no one in charge?
questions.answer: The left-hand road.

questions.question: What mistake did the second soldier make after hearing the warning?
questions.answer: He still chose the wrong road.

questions.question: What burden did the first soldier carry on his back?
questions.answer: A moderate load of supplies and a weapon.

questions.question: What heavier burdens did the second soldier carry in his heart?
questions.answer: Fear and the feeling of owing everyone.

questions.question: How did the second soldier act toward people on the road?
questions.answer: He begged from them.

questions.question: How did he react to things around him?
questions.answer: He was frightened by them.

questions.question: What do the words punished and rewarded show in this story?
questions.answer: They show that our choices lead to results.

questions.question: What is the main topic of this passage?
questions.answer: It teaches about the good of worship and the harm of wrongdoing.

questions.question: How many soldiers are in the comparison story?
questions.answer: Two.

questions.question: What happened to their one road as they traveled?
questions.answer: It split into two roads.

questions.question: Who spoke to them there?
questions.answer: A man at the fork.

questions.question: What did he say about the right road and peace of mind?
questions.answer: He said most people on it had calm hearts.

questions.question: What did he say about the left road and advantage?
questions.answer: He said it gave no real benefit.

questions.question: Why might someone be fooled into choosing the left road?
questions.answer: It looks easier because there is less to carry.

questions.question: Why is that ease called deceptive?
questions.answer: Because it seems good at first but leads to trouble.

questions.question: What did the fortunate soldier accept for the sake of the better road?
questions.answer: He accepted carrying the extra load.

questions.question: What did that choice save him from inside?
questions.answer: Great fear and feeling dependent on others.

questions.question: What did the other soldier reject?
questions.answer: He rejected army order and discipline.

questions.question: What happened to him because of that choice during the trip?
questions.answer: He became afraid and needy.

questions.question: What happened to him at the end because he had deserted?
questions.answer: He was punished.

questions.question: What happened to the soldier who stayed faithful to his duty?
questions.answer: He reached the city safely and received honor.
